subject: Post-call: Orion HealthTech inference SLOs & next technical steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@orionhealthtech.com>, Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@orionhealthtech.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-22T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call: Orion HealthTech inference SLOs & next technical steps

Hi Daniel / Sophie — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Call highlights (my notes):
- Primary goal: reduce per-request median latency to <120ms for 512-token inference across enterprise-grade EHR lookups, with 95th percentile under 350ms.
- Current constraints: Orion runs mixed-criticality queries (diagnostic summarization + clinical search) with bursty peaks during morning rounds (~2.5x baseline).
- Model preference: open LLM family (LlamaX-7B equivalent) with a plan to evaluate a quantized 4-bit variant.
- Data residency: US-only; some PHI in prompts so Private deployment (VPC) likely required.
- Success metrics: latency SLOs, token cost per request, and throughput target of 300 concurrent inference sessions during peak.

Immediate asks / next steps I propose:
1) Dev deep-dive: schedule 60-min architecture session with your infra/dev team and our infra lead (Dev). Goal: walk topology, traffic profiles, and KV cache integration.
2) SLO matrix: we’ll share a draft SLO matrix (attached) mapping request types -> latency SLOs + tail targets and recommended batching profiles.
3) Security: Sophie, please confirm SOC2 baseline and expected audit evidence timeline; we’ll provision the Private playbook items.
4) POC proposal: 4-week POC with Redwood Private deployed into your VPC, initial single-model serving and load test plan.

Attachments: orion-slo-matrix.xlsx (draft), sample deploy diagram.

If that looks right I’ll loop in Dev with a few times for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cell: +1 415-555-0198

- The 300 concurrent sessions number is for the core triage flow; non-triage assistants are lower priority.
- We can scrub PHI for the POC but need the production cut to be in our VPC and KMS.
- SOC2 Type II in-place; we’ll share the cert and an initial evidence bundle (Sophie will follow up).

We’re good with the 60-min deep-dive. Available Thu 2027-02-24 10:00–12:00 PT or Fri 2027-02-25 13:00–15:00 PT.

Daniel / Sophie — thanks, and hi all. I’ll lead the deep-dive. High-level items I want to cover so we can scope the POC correctly:
- Expected request size distribution (median token length, 90th pct) and per-request KV cache hit-rate expectations.
- Acceptable batching latency tradeoffs (we can tune batching window to meet median but need to understand tail budget).
- Model variants and quantization: we’ll need sample model artifacts or model zoo references (LlamaX-7B equiv) to validate kernel selection.
- Network topology: will we run Redwood Private in your single-subnet VPC or across multiple AZs? Load-balancer config matters for cold start profiles.
- Monitoring hooks: span/tracing headers we need to ingest for per-request latency breakdowns.

I’ve attached a preliminary topology image and the SLO matrix Aisha referenced. For the deep-dive, please add an infra lead and someone who can speak to the tokenization/PII scrubbing logic.

Proposed times work for me — I’ll block Thu 2027-02-24 10:30 PT to align with Daniel’s window. If that’s good I’ll send an invite with an agenda.

Subject: Deep-dive agenda + POC checklist (follow-up)

Folks — attaching the agenda and a short POC checklist in the Drive link below. Quick summary of items I’ll present on the call:
1) Latency/throughput targets mapped to configuration knobs: batching window, KV cache warmup, autoscale sizing per GPU class.
2) Model profile: expected memory, token-latency per layer, and quantization impact (we’ll show 4-bit vs 8-bit perf).
3) Deployment topology options: single-AZ low-latency vs multi-AZ resilient with cross-AZ tail tradeoffs. Diagram attached.
4) Load-test plan and pass/fail criteria for SLO acceptance.

Action items before call (please):
- Orion: share a 24-hour sample traffic dump (anonymized) and token length histogram.
- Orion: confirm which KMS provider and whether HSM is required for key management.
- Redwood: we’ll prepare an estimated cost model for the POC and a proposed canary rollout for production.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3C4D-Orion-Playbook
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/orion/record/ORION-2027-01

See you Thu 2027-02-24 10:30 PT (invite sent).

— Dev
